text.text: Pillboxes can be quickly knocked out with a precision dive bomber strike or Demolition Charges.
Carrying too much in your backpack will reduce your weapon's accuracy and your movement speed.
Going prone or diving can save your life from the effects of Explosives.
Killing enemies in melee combat rewards additional experience.
The crosshair gives a good estimate of accuracy, but your weapon's muzzle velocity has an additional impact as the range to your target increases.
Capturing a base requires a majority of troops, shown as 2/3 bars in the capture progress indicator.
Light Machine Guns are best fired from prone or over cover, and some of these weapons can only fire from those stances.
Selling briefcases at the Armoury will unlock rare weapons and equipment, but what you get is random!
Rifles are deadly and accurate, but fire slowly. Use caution when fighting in close range against better armed enemies. Bayonets can help!
Sniper Rifles are excellent at taking out the heavily-armoured Sentry soldiers from a distance.
Sniper Rifles have excellent accuracy when crouching, prone, or firing over cover; the standing posture does not offer superb precision.
Sniper Rifles extend your vision sight while standing still, but have several disadvantages, such as slow recoil recovery and poor accuracy when standing upright. Crouch or use cover!
Carbines offer decent long-range performance for a sidearm weapon, but often don't pack as much short-range power as Pistols.
Medium MGs usually offer a lot of long-range firepower, but since they can only be fired while laying prone or over cover, are better suited for 'bite-and-hold' tactics.
Weapons with an icon that shows a bayonet can mount one. Bayonets extend melee range, but also worsen your accuracy when standing still. Use wisely!
Valuables that are dropped by dead soldiers can be looted and stored in Stashes to sell later.
Sub-Machine Guns are unparalleled in close-quarters fighting and firing on the move, but suffer at long range.
In general, the heavier the weapon, the lower your movement speed.
Flamethrowers excel at clearing out strongpoints and well-defended emplacements, including pillboxes, and can even damage most vehicles.
Landing Craft have spawn points, provided that enemies aren't nearby.
The enemy will often utilize emplaced AA Guns on the map - destroy all of them to gain access to air support calls!
The enemy will often utilize emplaced Coastal Guns - destroy all of them gain access to naval artillery calls!
Armories have changed from Running with Rifles - they now visually resemble half-length 'Quonset Huts.'
Be on the lookout for enemy Specialist soldiers - they're tougher and come armed with better weapons. Their appearances will be distinct from regular infantry.
When a beach landing gets tough, look for the supporting guns on the Attack Ship - use them to bombard the beach defenses!
There are Armories and Stashes located on both the Aircraft Carrier and the Attack Ship, be sure to find their locations!
The specialized Assault Troops rush towards their enemy with no regard for cover, firing on the move and trying to get into melee range.
Banzai Chargers are ferocious Assault Troops lead be a Katana-wielding Officer, operating as a squad.
Enemy Flamethrower Operators are resilient against small arms, but are vulnerable to grenades, explosives, melee attacks, and even anti-tank rifles.
Bayonets extend melee range at a slight cost to long-range accuracy, as a result of the extra weight on the front of the gun.
The valued price of a weapon is often a good estimator as to both its rarity and combat effectiveness.
Binoculars are a great tool for high-ranking Officers - allowing them to command troops and call in Artillery on more distant locations.
The PT Boat is excellent in providing supporting fire on a beachhead with its vast array of weapons systems.
Destroy any enemy structures to decrease their fighting capacity.
Friendly soldiers and players you kill will not drop their gear. And, if you are accidently teamkilled, you will respawn with all of what you died with!
Eventually, rare weapons and gear on the ground will vanish - but rare weapons will stay on the field far longer.
Not all weapons have a 100% chance to drop when an enemy soldier is killed.
Sentry soldiers are rare specialist troops that spawn with a hip-fired Machine Gun and a thick set of Body Armour. They are highly-resistant to small-arms, and to some extent, explosives.
There are various items available in the 'Vest' category, each offering unique advantages. However if you die wearing a vest, you will not respawn with it!
The Veteran 'vest' grants additional resilience to enemy fire, and when you run out of 'luck', you might still enter a wounded state from which comrades can revive you.
The Banzai and Assault 'vests' grant additional resilience and a large bonus to movement speed, but unlike the higher-tier Veteran 'vest', you will die instead of entering a wounded state.
The Sniper 'vest' makes you harder to detect, and very slightly harder to hit. This bonus is of course particularly useful when using a Sniper Rifle.
The Sentry 'vest' is a heavy set of Body Armour. It offers good protection and enables you to become wounded instead of dying, but impairs movement speed and is markedly expensive.
You can always open the map when you die to select your spawn point.
In missions in which your faction is able to paradrop onto the field, you can open the map after dying and spawn behind enemy lines.
Anti-Tank Rifle Grenades have infinite ammo but only provide minimum damage. They can be used as a long-term anti-armour solution, but do little up front.
Some Anti-Tank Grenades explode on impact, while others stick to the target and explode after a few seconds.
While most Rocket Launchers perform about the same, some trade velocity for extra damage and blast radius.
Radio Jammers, Coastal Guns, and Anti-Air Guns block certain call-ins. Destroy them for a reward and to be able to call in power support fire!
Certain Missions may prevent calling in Air Support or Paratroopers, such as in the winter conditions at Bastogne.
Certain enemy assets like Water Towers or docked Submarines offer large XP and RP rewards for destroying them.
You can repair vehicles with a wrench by equipping it, standing close to the vehicle, and holding the 'attack' key until the work is done.
Anti-Tank Guns, though only encountered on certain Missions, do what they say on the tin - and excel at it.
